sources.headline: 12 killed, 29 injured as truck runs over devotees walking towards temple in Gwalior
14 killed, 28 injured as truck hits devotees near temple in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior
sources.content: In a horrific accident in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior, 13 people were killed and 28 others were injured after a truck rammed into devotees and shops when they were waiting near a temple.  The incident happened at around 1:30 am on the Sheetlamata Mandir road when the truck driver lost control and the vehicle hit devotees before coming to a halt by smashing into the temple wall, which led to a collapse. Kolkata Durga Puja stampede: Police detain 12, including organisersAn investigator said the truck’s brakes may have failed, forcing the driver to swerve left in a desperate attempt to control the vehicle. Had it continued straight, he said, it would have ploughed into at least 600 to 700 devotees.The truck driver fled from the spot, and police teams were searching for him.The accident has raised concerns about security arrangements at the shrine, as the truck, with a Punjab registration number, entered the no-entry zone, officials told PTI.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the loss of lives and announced ex gratia relief of Rs 2 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased and Rs 50,000 for each injured.“Distressed to learn about the loss of lives due to a mishap in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. My condolences to the bereaved families. Praying for the speedy recovery of the injured,” Modi said in an X post.Rescue operations are underway under the supervision of senior officials.

stories.primary_headline: Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede

primary_source.headline: Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede
primary_source.content: The stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata claimed the lives of 19 people, while 25 others were injured. A senior police officer told PTI that lack of crowd management and misleading announcements following sudden heavy rainfall during Saptami celebrations could have led to the tragic incident. Police also found that the number of police personnel and private security guards deployed at the venue was inadequate, worsening the situation."We have gathered sufficient evidence pointing to gross mismanagement by the puja organisers. There was no clear plan to manage the large number of visitors, and everything was handled verbally. We have collected CCTV camera footage, recorded accounts from locals and eyewitnesses, and corroborated our findings. Security personnel were inadequate," the police officer told PTI.At least 19 dead, 25 others injured in stampede-like situation at Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata"Due to the mismanagement, people tried to escape through the entrance gate during the stampede. Both the gates and the approach road were narrow, which contributed to the accident," he said, adding that announcements regarding entry, exit and crowd movement were misleading, leaving visitors confused during the rush."We have video footage of an announcement asking people to leave the pandal on the grounds that the structure was about to collapse. We are trying to identify who made the announcement and what prompted it," the officer said.Moreover, the locals also claimed that police deployment was inadequate, alleging that personnel were mainly stationed near the VIP entrance.A team of forensic experts visited the pandal on Saturday night and collected evidence from the site, he said."Another team of forensic experts will visit the pandal today to collect further evidence. Officers from our Detective Department will also visit the venue as part of the investigation," he said.The Kolkata Police could question survivors as part of the probe, the IPS officer said."We need first-hand accounts to cross-check the findings based on statements from locals and other eyewitnesses. This will help our investigation," he added.Meanwhile, prohibitory orders under Section 163 have been imposed on roads adjoining the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Sunday morning.The order prohibits gatherings on roads surrounding the venue, which falls under the jurisdiction of Bowbazar Police Station. The restrictions will remain in force until October 20.Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that the state government would provide Rs 25 lakh in compensation and a Group D government job to the family of each deceased victim.He also ordered the formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court, to investigate the incident.

sources.headline: India bars sugarcane-based ethanol from 2026-27 procurement tender to safeguard sugar supplies
sources.content: New Delhi: State-run oil marketing companies have excluded ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from their latest procurement tender for the 2026-27 supply year, following government directions to halt sugar diversion for fuel amid concerns over domestic availability and prices.Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), acting on behalf of the oil marketing companies, issued the tender on October 16 seeking bids for approximately 11 billion litres of ethanol. The volume is intended to support the nationwide target of blending 20 per cent ethanol in petrol during the supply year that runs from November 2026 to October 2027.The tender document states: “The Government of India has issued directions that sugar diversion for ethanol be reduced to zero for ethanol supply year 2026-27.” It adds that “no offers have been sought for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar or sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses.”Instead, the companies will accept bids for ethanol made from maize, broken rice, surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India, and C-heavy molasses. The procurement price for maize-based ethanol has also been reduced to Rs 68.86 per litre from Rs 71.86, cutting the incentive from Rs 5.79 to Rs 2.79 per litre.Sugar, ethanol and the policy balance: Why India needs predictable rules over crisis controlsThe restrictions come after poor rainfall in major sugar-producing states such as Maharashtra and Karnataka raised the prospect of lower output. India, the world’s largest sugar consumer, has faced rising domestic prices and concerns that continued diversion of cane and sugar into ethanol could tighten food supplies.The ethanol-blended petrol programme has relied on both sugarcane- and grain-based feedstock to cut crude oil imports and reduce vehicle emissions. India has rolled out E20 fuel — petrol containing up to 20 per cent ethanol — as the national standard. Officials view the latest tender as an effort to maintain the blending targets while prioritising sugar availability for consumption and containing prices.

sources.content: The tender, issued on October 16 by Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) on behalf of oil marketing companies (OMCs), seeks bids for around 11 billion litres of ethanol for the supply year beginning November to meet the requirement of doping 20 per cent ethanol in petrol.

sources.headline: CJP alleges delay in release of leaders, 4 sureties rejected
sources.content: New Delhi: The bail hearing of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka was "delayed" on Sunday as the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) did not arrive at the scheduled time, activist Ratna Singh said and alleged that four sureties had been rejected on "vague" grounds.Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody on October 14 after they entered Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, by scaling its locked gates. The CJP leaders maintained that they had unfurled the national flag and raised slogans.In a post on X, Singh said she had been at the police station since 11 am, while the hearing was scheduled for noon. She said the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP/SEM) had not arrived at the Mandir Marg police station by 4.42 pm.CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde under preventive arrest; likely to be produced before magistrate"This is really concerning. They have rejected 4 sureties till now on vague reasons. They have made people who have FIRs against them for being part of protest as people having criminal antecedents (sic)," Singh alleged.There was no response from police on the allegations.In another post, Singh said, "Unfurling the Indian National Flag is not a crime, and the boys should not remain in custody due to procedural delays."Questioning the functioning of the SEM courts in the national capital, Singh said higher courts had asked authorities to follow the hierarchy and alleged an "absolute misuse of power".On Saturday, the CJP said in a post on X that it had consulted senior advocate Kapil Sibal and warned of legal action if Das and Ranka were not released by Sunday."If Ashu and Saurav are not released by tomorrow, we will pursue legal action against all those who deliberately ensured that they continue to be in illegal custody, especially when they have not committed nor charged with any offence," the outfit had said."The deliberate use of delaying tactics to keep them behind bars cannot go unchallenged. Those responsible will be held accountable," it added.The outfit has been protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that the exercise threatens voters' rights.

stories.primary_headline: '56-inch ka seena kahan hai': Rahul Gandhi slams Modi-Shah, CEC over 'vote chori'

primary_source.headline: '56-inch ka seena kahan hai': Rahul Gandhi slams Modi-Shah, CEC over 'vote chori'
primary_source.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of orchestrating alleged “vote theft” behind the scenes, claiming that Union Home Minister Amit Shah operationalised it and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar implemented it.Addressing a rally in Margao in South Goa on the concluding day of the Congress's 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', Gandhi alleged that Modi, Shah and Kumar were facing mounting pressure over the party's allegations of electoral malpractice.“There is no confusion anymore. Gyanesh Kumar implements the vote theft, Amit Shah operationalises it, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi does the entire planning from behind the scenes,” Gandhi said.The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha warned that the three would face justice over the alleged irregularities. He also claimed that the Congress had evidence of electoral malpractice in several states, including Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Assam.“PM Modi, Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar will face justice and pay the price for what they have done,” he said.Gandhi had led protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and Kumar in New Delhi. He alleged that opposition votes had been deleted, votes added in favour of the ruling party, and voters shifted between districts or brought in from other states.Claiming that more than 45 defamation cases had been filed against him, including by people associated with Modi and Shah, Gandhi said no case had been filed over his allegations of vote theft. He suggested that the government was reluctant to pursue the matter legally because it could lead to a full-fledged legal battle.Urging voters to give the Congress a full majority in the 2027 Goa Assembly elections, Gandhi called on party workers to continue engaging with people across the state.Rahul Gandhi to address Goa rally as Congress wraps up 28-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra'“You think about Goa. In Delhi, in a short while, we will deal with Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. You don't need to worry about that. The work is underway; their expiry date is approaching,” he said.Gandhi also accused the BJP-led Union government of favouring industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani by awarding them infrastructure projects, land and other economic opportunities in exchange for political support and publicity.“This is their system. This is how their system works: give billionaires money, give them contracts, give them land. In return, the billionaires do their marketing,” he alleged.Turning to Goa, Gandhi accused the state government of taking land from farmers and economically weaker sections and transferring it to outsiders and associates. He alleged that the cancellation of the regional master plan had enabled the government to facilitate such transfers, putting the state's natural resources and cultural heritage at risk.“Goa is a paradise, one of the most beautiful places in the country, with a great culture,” he said, alleging that its land was being handed over to billionaires.The Congress leader further claimed that Goa had the country's highest unemployment rate, forcing young people to seek opportunities abroad. He accused the BJP government of dismantling the state's employment structure and described its functioning as a “special Goa model of corruption”, drawing a comparison with the Gujarat model associated with Modi.On education, Gandhi criticised the alleged use of force against student protesters in Delhi and accused the BJP and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of influencing university appointments. He said students were raising concerns over electoral malpractice, unemployment, education costs and inflation.“This country does not belong to any one organisation. This country does not belong to the RSS. This country does not belong to the BJP. This country belongs to the people of India,” he said.Gandhi added that Goa belonged to its people, not its chief minister or ministers, and called for access to education, healthcare and employment, alongside environmental protection.Taking a swipe at the Prime Minister, Gandhi questioned the absence of Modi's often-cited “56-inch seena”, saying he could not stand in front of his political opponents.He urged Congress workers to continue the party's fight against the BJP's ideology beyond the conclusion of the yatra.The 27-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', led by Goa Congress leaders Yuri Alemao and Girish Chodankar, began on September 22 and covered all 40 Assembly constituencies in the coastal state. The party said the campaign aimed to protect Goa's land, environment, cultural heritage and identity while strengthening its grassroots presence ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.(With PTI Inputs)

stories.primary_headline: Explained | Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA

primary_source.headline: Explained | Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA
primary_source.content: The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers has announced a price cap of 30 per cent on the trade margins of 137 cancer medicines, over the cost of the drug at the first point, either to a stockist/distributor or the hospital. These margins will apply when the drugs are sold directly to them by a manufacturer.&nbsp;The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), in an order dated October 17, has directed manufacturers to submit the revised MRP within seven days. "The revised prices shall come into effect from November 9," the gazette notification stated.&nbsp;Impact on cancer drug pricesAn analysis of pharmaceutical market data indicates that non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs carry an average trade mark-up of approximately 170 per cent, with mark-ups of up to 700 per cent in certain cases, according to an NPPA meeting conducted earlier. This order is expected to reduce the MRP of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs by 70 per cent, depending on their current price structures.&nbsp;The 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs include immunotherapy drugs used for treating over 20 types of cancers, denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, pegfilgrastim, which is used to prevent neutropenia in cancer patients and bevacizumab, which is the approved drug to treat colon, ovarian, and cervical cancer. With this notification, MRP of widely used anti-cancer drugs such as pembrolizumab, durvalumab and osimertinib is expected to become more accessible for cancer patients.Anti-cancer drug prices to come down as govt caps trade margins at 30%Centre caps trade margins on cancer medicines at 30% of MRPMarket overview: scheduled vs non-scheduled drugsCurrently, the anti-cancer drugs market comprises nearly 225 drugs and 500 formulations, with an annual turnover of around Rs 12,500 crore. Of this, scheduled cancer drugs that come under price control account for approximately Rs 2,250 crore, with the balance comprising non-scheduled drugs.To ensure that these life-saving medicines remain available, manufacturers of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs will be required to maintain their current production levels. NPPA has clearly stated: "The manufacturers of the formulations are required to maintain the present production levels. Any manufacturer intending to lower the average monthly production levels will seek prior permission from NPPA. Further, any manufacturer intending to discontinue production of the above-said formulations shall furnish information to NPPA."&nbsp;How is the new price calculated?The manufacturers of non–scheduled formulations, selling branded or generic or both the versions of formulations at MRP higher than the MRP should revise their prices using this formula:&nbsp; MRP of the product = Price to Stockist or Price to Distributor x {1 + (Trade Margin/(100 − Trade Margin))} + Applicable GST.&nbsp;Citing an example, NPPA explained: For a non-scheduled anti-cancer formulation with current MRP: Rs 300 + Applicable GST. However, the price to a distributor is Rs 70. Maximum allowable revised MRP as per formula shall be: Rs70x{1+(30/(100−30))} = Rs 100 + Applicable GST.&nbsp;The notification has also clarified: "All the existing manufacturers of formulations having MRP lower than the MRP so computed … shall maintain their existing MRP."

New Delhi: As the Election Commission "resumes" distribution of "readable" electoral rolls to parties after a "gap of eight years", Congress on Sunday said "nothing can save" Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar while insisting that a "thorough" revamp of the poll body and its IT system is required.General Secretary (Communications) Jairam Ramesh said the decision to provide electoral rolls in readable PDF format  was the result of the whole nation being on the streets against the "vote chors".EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23The attack comes as the Congress prepares to host I.N.D.I.A. bloc parties at a rally in Ramlila Maidan on November 1 against the CEC.In a post on 'X', he said over the past two years, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have been "persistent, insistent and consistent" in demanding that the EC provide electoral rolls in searchable format to all parties. पिछले दो वर्षों से लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता श्री राहुल गांधी और कांग्रेस पार्टी लगातार, मजबूती से और पुरजोर तरीके से यह मांग करते आ रहे हैं कि भारत निर्वाचन आयोग सभी राजनीतिक दलों को मतदाता सूची ऐसे डिजिटल फॉर्मेट में उपलब्ध कराए, जिसमें मतदाताओं के नाम और अन्य जानकारी आसानी से…&mdash; Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) October 18, 2026
 

"The demand was repeatedly refused by the ECI - which stopped providing searchable voter rolls in 2018 when the Congress found lakhs of bogus voters in Madhya Pradesh. The demand was denied for eight years to enable 'vote chori'," he claimed.Referring to the October 15 announcement by the EC on providing voter lists in readable format, he said "every time Vote Chori is caught, the Modi government adopts a new tactic: stopping readable voter rolls, fake voter additions, SIR. But not this time.""Nothing can save the CEC Gyanesh Kumar who, acting on the instructions of the PM and the HM, has destroyed public trust and confidence in the ECI. He simply has to go. But that alone will not be enough. The ECI itself along with its IT system has to be thoroughly revamped," he said. TThe SIR, that has put the Constitutional right to vote for over 13 crore Indians at risk, has to be suspended forthwith, he added.

sources.headline: EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23
sources.content: New Delhi: The 'People Against SIR', a coalition of various organisations, on Sunday announced a ‘People’s March to Reclaim Democracy’ on October 23 across India demanding removal and prosecution of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, scrapping of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and restoration of voters whose names have been deleted.With the slogan ‘Har Haath Mein Tiranga, Har Gali Jantar Mantar’ (In Every Hand Tricolor, Every Street is Jantar Mantar), the coalition of civil society organisations, farmer unions, trade unions, students and youth organisations, academicians, artistes and activists said the protest marches with tricolor in their hands will be held at tehsil, district, state and national level.Nothing can save CEC; SIR must be suspended forthwith: CongressThe coalition, which included actor-activist Prakash Raj, Kisan Sabha leader P Krishnaprasad and CPI(ML)L leader N Sai Balaji, said the ‘People's March’ will not request police permission anywhere while "strictly warning" police, paramilitary and prisons against using the "brute state force" against peaceful protesters.&nbsp;If the march is blocked by police, it said, the protesters will peacefully hold the People's Parliament and disperse later after singing the national anthem.Claiming that the CEC helped the BJP to remain in power, it recalled that the Supreme Court has maintained that it did not upheld alteration of Form 6 used for inclusion of new voters.&nbsp;“Gyanesh Kumar has violated his Constitutional pledge and must be prosecuted. But the Prime Minister himself is protecting the criminal...Without Parliament impeaching CEC Gyanesh Kumar, the Prime Minister cannot come out of the full-blown constitutional standoff,” it said.Calling upon farmers, workers, daily wage earners, traders, entrepreneurs, journalists, advocates, teachers, employees, artists, intellectuals, women, youth, students, adivasis, dalits and minorities to join the march, a statement said its demands include comprehensive electoral reforms, proportional representation, curb money/muscle power and legalise state funding of polls.The statement alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have misused the Election Commission and erased the voting rights of 13.41 crore citizens through SIR.

stories.primary_headline: Durga Puja pandal stampede gives Mamata's TMC a ‘bhaipo’ in BJP to target

primary_source.headline: Durga Puja pandal stampede gives Mamata's TMC a ‘bhaipo’ in BJP to target
primary_source.content: Kolkata: The stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata has triggered a war of words in West Bengal politics, as the alleged association of two ruling Bharatiya Janata Party leaders and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari’s nephew with the organisers provided fresh ammunition to the Mamata Banerjee faction of the Trinamool Congress to attack the government.Suvendu, himself, on October 12, inaugurated the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity’s pandal, where a stampede left 19 people dead and more than 20 injured on Sunday. The narrow entry and exit alleyways, limited space and inadequate crowd-control measures, deliberately dim lighting to match the pandal's theme, a sudden influx of visitors seeking shelter from the evening rain, and alleged lapses in police arrangements are blamed for the disaster.With Suvendu’s nephew, Debdeep Adhikari, being the chief patron of the organising committee, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, the TMC faction led by Mamata Banerjee, finally found a ‘bhaipo’ in the ruling BJP to train the guns on.&nbsp;“Guess who is closely associated with the Chorebagan Puja Pandal? CM Suvendu Adhikari’s BHAIPO,” the MAITC posted on X soon after the disaster. “When are you going to put your criminal nephew behind bars, Suvendu Babu?” posted Abhishek Banerjee, who has been at the receiving end of the ‘bhaipo (nephew)’ taunt ever since his ‘pisi (aunt)’, Mamata Banerjee, inducted him into the party she founded.The tragedy raised questions about whether the organisers had made adequate safety arrangements for the large crowds expected at the pandal. Its narrow entry and exit passageways, sloping route through the structure, and deliberately dim lighting intended to complement its theme may have heightened the risk of overcrowding and slowed visitor movement. The sudden influx of people seeking shelter from the evening rain further compounded the danger, while questions were raised about the police's preparedness to regulate the crowds and respond to the emergency.Not only Debdeep, but two other BJP leaders were also associated with this year’s Durga Puja of the Chorebagan Sarbojanin Durgotsav Samity, legislator Vijay Ojha as chairman and the saffron party’s North Kolkata district unit president, Tamoghna Ghosh, as chief adviser.The six people arrested by police after the incident include the secretary Raj Kumar Sewda and the vice president of the organising committee Santanu Dubey, but none are linked to the BJP.“The CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan Puja Pandal. Did he not look into security arrangements when he visited the pandal? Won’t he be held accountable for every single life lost?” the Mamata faction of the TMC asked, questioning whether the police would take any action against Debdeep, Vijay and Tamoghna.Soon after the stampede on Saturday, Suvendu and Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee rushed to Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, where the injured and deceased were initially taken. The chief minister visited the stampede site in the pre-dawn hours of Sunday.“Attempts are being made by some people to reap political dividends from such a tragedy. They will not succeed. The families of the deceased and injured told me that they had full faith in the state government and me,” Suvendu said on Sunday. He added that a probe was underway and the government would not spare anyone found responsible for the disaster. “No one should indulge in politics over death,” he said.&nbsp;Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govtHe sought to turn the tables on his predecessor, Mamata Banerjee, and the TMC government she had headed.&nbsp;The chief minister cited several tragedies during the TMC’s tenure, including the collapse of an under-construction flyover in north Kolkata in 2016, which killed seven people, and the collapse of Majherhat Bridge in 2018, which killed three. He also referred to the Panihati festival incident in July 2022, in which three people died; the electrocution deaths of nine people during waterlogging in Kolkata after heavy rain ahead of Durga Puja in 2025; and flash floods in North Bengal that year, which killed around 100 people.“What was the then chief minister doing?” Suvendu questioned, hitting back at Mamata.&nbsp;“This is not the time to indulge in a political blame game,” Samik Bhattacharya, the state BJP chief, said, responding to the Opposition's criticism. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Opposition, however, is not ready to relent. “Where were the police when the incident took place? There was no response even after calls were made to the police control room,” Subhankar Sarkar, president of the West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee, said.What further sharpened criticism of the city police and the state government is that, over the past few days, cops in several places were seen evicting or trying to evict bookstalls set up by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) near the Durga Puja pandals. stories.primary_headline: Gwalior temple tragedy: MP CM orders removal of SP, suspension of 8 other police personnel

primary_source.headline: Gwalior temple tragedy: MP CM orders removal of SP, suspension of 8 other police personnel
primary_source.content: Bhopal: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday ordered the removal of the Gwalior City Superintendent of Police and the suspension of eight other personnel after the temple accident that claimed 14 lives when a truck ploughed into devotees.The speeding truck ran over several devotees outside the Sheetla Mata temple in Gwalior district early Sunday and then rammed into its entrance gate, killing 14 persons and injuring 28 others, including two police personnel, officials said. Seven of those injured were in critical condition.A wall of the temple crashed under the impact of the collision, they said.'Came like a storm': Eyewitnesses recall truck's deadly dash towards Gwalior templeThe incident, which occurred around 1.30 am outside the temple near a slope on Chinor Road, raised concerns about security arrangements at the shrine, as the truck, with a Punjab registration number, entered the no-entry zone, officials said."The accident occurred because the truck entered a prohibited area," Yadav told reporters in Indore.The chief minister said he had directed the district administration to conduct a fact-based inquiry and submit a report.Later, in a post on X, Yadav said his government has ordered the removal of the Gwalior CSP from his post and the suspension of three station house officers, a traffic inspector, a head constable and three constables.A detailed inquiry has been ordered to fix responsibility and ensure strict action against those found guilty, he said."The safety of all citizens is paramount. To prevent the recurrence of such incidents in future, security arrangements will be reviewed and necessary steps taken. No negligence will be tolerated at any level in public safety," he said.Yadav also announced compensation of Rs 4 lakh each for the kin of the deceased and said the government would bear the treatment expenses of those seriously injured in the accident. The persons who suffered minor injuries would receive financial assistance of Rs 50,000 each, he added.The impact brought down a temple wall, trapping people under the debris.The bodies and injured persons were shifted to different hospitals, including Gwalior's trauma centre.Relatives of victims gathered near the post-mortem facility at the trauma centre and expressed anger over the incident, with many questioning how a heavy truck could enter an area where, they claimed, even a bicycle could not pass.Lokendra Singh Tomar, nephew of the deceased Sarla Tomar, asked how the truck was allowed to enter the temple premises despite security arrangements.14 killed, 28 injured as truck hits devotees near temple in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior His aunt was on her way to offer prayers at the shrine, he told reporters and demanded answers from those responsible for the accident.Pawan Rathore (23), a resident of Gadaipur in Gwalior’s Hazira area, was among those killed. His family took the body away amid inconsolable grief. He had gone to the temple to offer prayers when the accident occurred.Sandeep, a relative of injured devotee Nikesh, said the family received a phone call around 5 am informing them that Nikesh had been hurt at the temple. When they reached the hospital, he was in critical condition with both legs fractured and was placed on a ventilator, he added.

primary_source.headline: Attacked from the sky: Sudanese goldminers count deadly cost of eking out a living on the Egypt border
primary_source.content: As civil war has left their country in ruins, many young Sudanese have turned to artisanal mining. An airstrike on a mine last week killed more than 100 and has provoked anger against Egypt, seen as the most likely suspectTorches still fixed on their heads but tools cast aside, the Sudanese goldminers of the North Valley had already mounted an impromptu rescue operation by the time Ammar* arrived at the site of a suspected Egyptian airstrike.At least 114 were killed, according to the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers, in the strike on Saturday 10 October on an artisanal goldmine brimming with young Sudanese trying to eke out a living in a country where the economy has been shattered by three years of war. An airstrike on a mine last week killed more than 100 and has provoked anger against Egypt, seen as the most likely suspectTorches still fixed on their heads but tools cast aside, the Sudanese goldminers of the North Valley had already mounted an impromptu rescue operation by the time Ammar* arrived at the site of a suspected Egyptian airstrike.At least 114 were killed, according to the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers, in the strike on Saturday 10 October on an artisanal goldmine brimming with young Sudanese trying to eke out a living in a country where the economy has been shattered by three years of war. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg

primary_source.headline: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
primary_source.content: The St Petersburg Oil Terminal was among targets hit in the city overnight The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five. A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit. Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week. Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing. It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

stories.primary_headline: Five killed after car, trying to escape pothole, crashes into state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed

primary_source.headline: Five killed after car, trying to escape pothole, crashes into state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed
primary_source.content: Beed: Five people, among them an 11-year-old boy, were killed after their car swerved to avoid potholes and collided with a state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed district on Sunday morning, police said.The accident occurred around 11 am at Shindewadi Cross Road on the Khamgaon-Pandharpur National Highway in Majalgaon tehsil, around 55 km from the district headquarters, an official said.He said that the victims, all residents of Majalgaon, were travelling towards Tuljapur in neighbouring Dharashiv district when their car crashed into a Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) bus coming from the opposite direction.The collision reduced the car to a mangled heap of metal, killing all five occupants on the spot, the official said.According to the police, the deceased have been identified as Omkar Mahadev Giri (24), Gajanan Mahadev Namdas (38), his son Samarth (11), Somnath Bade (23), and Anil Acharya (40).Speeding car crash triggers communal, moral and political row in KeralamCCTV footage from the area showed the speeding car lose control while attempting to avoid potholes on a bridge, leading to the head-on crash with the bus, the official said.The fatal crash triggered public anger over the deteriorating condition of roads on the Majalgaon-Telgaon stretch. Locals staged a road blockade alleging that substandard construction and poor maintenance had left fissures and uneven surfaces across the highway, turning the arterial road into an accident zone.Traffic came to a standstill for several hours on the highway due to the protest before senior police and district officials arrived at the scene, pacified the protesters, and restored traffic flow.

stories.primary_headline: Ebola outbreak spreads to eighth province in DR Congo, death toll tops 4,500

primary_source.headline: Ebola outbreak spreads to eighth province in DR Congo, death toll tops 4,500
primary_source.content: The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, Congo's public health institute said on Sunday, confirming earlier Reuters reporting.The emergence of cases in the province, which borders Central African Republic, poses a new challenge for health authorities struggling to contain the outbreak.The National Institute for Biomedical Research confirmed two cases - including one death - in North Ubangi.Reuters reported on Thursday that two cases were confirmed in the province, citing two health officials. At the time, there was no official statement by Congolese authorities.WHO says Congo Ebola outbreak can still be brought under control within three monthsNorth Ubangi becomes the eighth province affected by the outbreak, alongside North Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, Sud-Kivu, Bas-Uele and South Ubangi.The outbreak, the worst Ebola epidemic in Congo's history, has already spread beyond the country's borders, with cases recorded in Uganda and seven infections confirmed in Kenya this month.Congo's latest situation report showed 67 new confirmed cases and 26 new deaths in the 24 hours to Oct.16, bringing the cumulative total to 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths since the outbreak began.The outbreak remains concentrated in eastern Congo, with Ituri province reporting 44 of the 67 new cases.

stories.primary_headline: NHS data breaches a disgrace, says health secretary

primary_source.headline: NHS data breaches a disgrace, says health secretary
primary_source.content: Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates were killed in the Nottingham attacks Speaking to the BBC, Yvette Cooper said she expected action to be taken against staff who have breached NHS data and privacy standards. Dr Manjeet Shehmar, NUH medical director, previously said there was "simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason". Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper said "there's got to be proper respect for patients" from NHS staff. "Let me be really clear about this," she said. "There are proper data and privacy standards across the NHS. Students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020.

stories.primary_headline: Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govt

primary_source.headline: Kolkata stampede | 'CM himself inaugurated Chorebagan puja pandal, will he be held accountable?': Mamata AITC attacks Suvendu govt
primary_source.content:
Kolkata: The Mamata All India Trinamool Congress launched a sharp attack on West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and Kolkata Police over a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal that claimed 19 lives, bringing the name of the CM's nephew Debdeep Adhikari, listed as chief patron of the Chorbagan Sarbojonin Durgotsab Samity, under the spotlight.The opposition party questioned the preparedness of the authorities and alleged that inadequate crowd management, a lack of police presence and the absence of adequate emergency arrangements contributed to the tragedy at the popular Chorbagan pandal on Saturday evening.In a series of posts on social media, the Mamata AITC alleged there were no adequate police personnel, civic volunteers or ambulances at the venue when the situation spiralled out of control.It cited accounts of locals and eyewitnesses to question the security arrangements and the administration's response.Mismanagement, confusing announcements and narrow gates: What led to Kolkata pandal stampede"Where was the security and emergency response when people needed you most?" the party asked on its social media handles, targeting the Kolkata Police over the alleged lapses.The party's national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee also questioned the alleged involvement of the chief minister's nephew in the puja organising committee and demanded accountability from the ruling establishment.Referring to the committee's list of office-bearers, he asked, "When will you put the culprit nephew in jail, Suvendu Babu?"Will @KolkataPolice take any action against the first three names or are they being protected by the illegitimate CM himself?Debdeep Adhikari - Chief PatronNEPHEW OF @SuvenduWBVijay Ojha - Chairman@BJP4Bengal MLATamoghna Ghosh - Chief AdvisorBJP District President, North… https://t.co/5PMqi75arE pic.twitter.com/a7M5mjb9VQ&mdash; All India Trinamool Congress (@AITCofficial) October 18, 2026
 

In support of its claim, the party shared purported publicity material of the organising committee of the Chorbagan puja which listed Debdeep Adhikari as its chief patron, Vijay Ojha, the BJP MLA of the local Jorasanko constituency as the committee chairman and BJP's North Kolkata district president Tamaghna Ghosh as its chief advisor.It demanded that those connected with the event be held accountable.Mamata AITC spokesperson and MLA Kunal Ghosh further alleged that the previous puja committee was "forced" to step down following the change of guard in power, and was "captured" by a new committee.Ghosh posted on Facebook a letter, purportedly written by former puja secretary Jayanta Banerjee on July 17, tendering his resignation and relieving other committee members from their responsibilities."The previous committee in Chorbagan was allegedly forced to resign, following which a new set of people 'captured' the new committee. Take a look at the resignation letters of the former committee members and the list of members of the new committee," Ghosh wrote, bringing the puja committee's current leadership under scrutiny.Acting on a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder registered at the local Girish Park police station, law enforcers on Sunday arrested seven people, including the puja committee general secretary Raj Kumar Sewda and vice president Santanu Dubey.Responding to a question on the alleged involvement of Debdeep Adhikari in the affairs of the Chorbagan Puja, BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said he had no knowledge about the matter.Kolkata pandal stampede: Seven, including Chorbagan Durga Puja organisers, arrested"To the best of my knowledge, the chief minister's nephew is a minor and stays in Kanthi in Purba Medinipur district. How can he get involved in a Kolkata puja? I do not wish to indulge in politics over this tragedy. I am quite devastated at the scale of this horrible incident," Bhattacharya told reporters on Saturday evening after visiting the spot where the stampede took place.Adhikari, in a message on early Sunday morning, strongly condemned the attempts to politicise the tragedy and lashed out at critics, stating the entire top brass of the state police and administration was doing everything in its power to offer relief to the victims and their families."Without blaming anyone, I would say that last year there were two incidents, the first where 13 people died of electrocution in waterlogged areas and second, where over a hundred people were washed away in flash floods in the upper reaches of West Bengal. You had seen the role of the then chief minister at the time," Adhikari said."I am not comparing them with the current tragedy, only saying this because things are being written on social media. I will ask them to refrain from making such comments. People will spit on you; if you keep doing it," he added.The stampede unfolded around 7.30-7.40 pm on Saturday, as a large crowd gathered at the pandal amid rainfall. The crush occurred near an exit and a narrow approach lane, with the sudden rush and people falling over one another triggering chaos. The exact sequence of events and the possible role of crowd-control failures are being investigated.Adhikari, meanwhile, has announced a probe into the incident. Police detained organisers, private security personnel and others involved in managing the crowd for questioning, while investigators are examining possible lapses in security and the management of entry and exit routes.The chief minister has also said he would request the Calcutta High Court chief justice to facilitate an inquiry led by a judge.The state government has announced compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a government job for a member of each deceased person's family, besides Rs 5 lakh for each injured person and coverage of their medical expenses.The tragedy has cast a shadow over Durga Puja celebrations in the city, with the authorities moving to inspect other crowded pandals and review safety arrangements to prevent a recurrence.

stories.primary_headline: The playground murder - trauma, loss and a love that endured

primary_source.headline: The playground murder - trauma, loss and a love that endured
primary_source.content: Best friends Diane (left) and Pauline (right) did everything together Pauline watched as 16-year-old Diane collapsed after the knife attack by another pupil and then helped to carry her across the road to the arms of her parents who lived in an upstairs flat within view of the school. Diane's murder would not only devastate her family, her friends and the local community, its shockwaves would go on to be felt for decades. Diane Watson was 16 when she died Thirty-five years later, Pauline Love Thomson has spoken for the first time about the trauma of that April morning when she was just 16. Pauline describes how a large crowd of schoolkids gathered round as Glover shouted at Diane while waving the knife - and the chilling moment she dealt the deadly blow.

stories.primary_headline: Watch: Police hunt for synthetic drugs in Chicago jail

primary_source.headline: Watch: Police hunt for synthetic drugs in Chicago jail
primary_source.content: Chicago's largest jail, and the largest single use jail in America, is Cook County. In 2023 it saw a spike in overdose deaths. The facility, which averages one or two overdose deaths a year, lost eight inmates that year to fatal seizures. Security footage shows prisoners spasming and collapsing. Traditional drugs were usually brought into the jail in body cavities, so the jail had the same body scanners you find at airports to prevent that happening. However, a new way of drugs entering the prison was uncovered. Drugs were being mailed into the jail soaked in the paper of the pages of books and in letters. The BBC's Quentin Sommerville joined corrections officers at Cook County as they prepared for an early morning raid on the jail's high security D block. To understand the challenge that authorities face in tackling the problem the BBC interviewed a former inmate and dealer, who explained how synthetic drugs can be made in the US using household ingredients and how this could change the demand for drugs from outside of the country.

stories.primary_headline: Intensifying drone attacks on ships in Black Sea bring war ever closer to Nato shores

primary_source.headline: Intensifying drone attacks on ships in Black Sea bring war ever closer to Nato shores
primary_source.content: Six attacks in 10 days by suspected Russian drones mark dramatic escalation in maritime conflictThe first the crew of the Bulgarian ferry Dioscuria knew of an attack on a cargo ship in their country’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea in the early hours of 6 October was a distant explosion 70 miles off the coastal town of Byala.The Turkish-owned Alfa Watan, heading for the Romanian port of Sulina, had been struck by suspected Russian air and naval drones. Arriving on the scene, Dioscuria found an overturned lifeboat and lifejackets in the water. There was no sign, however, of Alfa Watan’s crew of 10. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Tamil Nadu: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes

primary_source.headline: Tamil Nadu: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes
primary_source.content: Ranipet (Tamil Nadu): Veteran Tamil music composer and singer Deva, popularly known as 'Thenisai Thendral', was laid to rest with full state honours at his family farmland in Sakkaramallur near Arcot, Ranipet district, on Sunday.He was 75.Deva died of a heart attack in Chennai on the morning of October 17.His mortal remains were taken from his Chennai residence to the farmland, where the final rites were performed.Thousands of people gathered at the site to pay their last respects to the celebrated music director.Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had visited Deva's residence in Chennai to pay his respects and announced that the funeral would be held with state honours in recognition of the composer's contribution to the music industry.Revenue and police officials oversaw arrangements for the ceremony at Sakkaramallur.‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva (1950-2026): The maestro who took gaana to the masses Relatives and villagers recalled Deva's enduring connection to his roots, saying he regularly visited his native village during festivals such as Pongal and contributed to local initiatives, including funding the construction of a Sri Ranganathar temple.Born Devanesan Chokkalingam, Deva had a career spanning nearly four decades and composed music for more than 400 films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.Before turning to films, Deva was an employee of the Tamil Nadu government’s Public Works Department (PWD).He made his entry as a composer in 1986 with 'Mattukkara Mannaru', which did not fare well in theatres, though its songs found a loyal audience over time.'Manasukketha Maharasa' (1989), starring Ramarajan and Seetha, was the film that first drew attention to his work. His real breakthrough, however, came in 1990 with the Prashanth-starrer 'Vaigasi Poranthachu', which won him widespread acclaim.Deva rose to prominence in the late 1980s and 1990s with his high-energy, folk-rooted tunes, and is widely credited with bringing the ‘gaana’ genre into mainstream Tamil cinema.Few composers in Tamil cinema are as closely identified with one genre as Deva is with 'gaana', the urban folk music born in the working-class neighbourhoods of North Chennai.He worked with nearly every leading star of his time, among them Vijayakanth, Sarathkumar, Vijay and Ajith, and delivered some of the biggest hits of their careers.Among his chartbusters were the Rajinikanth films ‘Annamalai’, ‘Baashha’ and ‘Arunachalam’, and the Kamal Haasan outings ‘Avvai Shanmugi’, ‘Pammal K Sambandam’ and ‘Panchathanthiram’.His death drew tributes from political leaders, members of the film fraternity and fans across Tamil Nadu.

stories.primary_headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues

primary_source.headline: One month of IIT Bombay student's death: No arrests yet; protest continues
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Exactly a month after Sahil Wakode, a student of Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay died by suicide, students and activists staged a protest outside the institute’s Powai campus on Sunday, however, police dispersed the mob and detained several of them.The parents of Sahil—Ravindra Wakode and Sonali Wakode—too were part of the protests.&nbsp;On 18 September, Sahil (20), a second-year student from Energy Science and Engineering Department, was caught allegedly using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination. However, his body was later found in his hostel room.&nbsp;The case is being investigated by the&nbsp;Crime Branch-CID, which has taken over investigations from the Powai police station.&nbsp;Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by policeThe parents are demanding action and arrest of&nbsp; Prof Shireesh Kedare, the Director of&nbsp; Indian Institute of Technology-Bombay and Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, a faculty member of the premier institute’s Energy Science and Engineering Department.Meanwhile, the Congress once again backed the parents and said that it will ensure that Sahil Wakode gets justice. Sahil Wakode, a backward-class student at the IIT Mumbai institution, did not commit suicide; it was "an institutional murder."“Even though a month has passed since this incident, no action has been taken against anyone yet. In the past 13 months, 4 students in this institution have died by suicide. After Sahil's death, students in the institution are protesting, and the police are committing atrocities against them, beating them. On whose orders are the police committing atrocities in the institution's premises? All these things must stop. An inquiry must be conducted quickly, and strict action must be taken against those responsible for Sahil's murder,” said Mumbai Congress president and MP Prof Varsha Gaikwad.&nbsp;“RSS ideology has infiltrated this prestigious IIT institution, and this is not good for the education sector. Keep educational institutions away from political ideologies,” she added.&nbsp;A delegation from the All India Independent Scheduled Castes Association arrived at the IIT Bombay gates around noon, seeking to pay respects to Sahil.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: ‘My time, my era’: Dubois sends out warning to rivals with Wardley demolition

primary_source.headline: ‘My time, my era’: Dubois sends out warning to rivals with Wardley demolition
primary_source.content: WBO heavyweight champion targets big paydays against Hrgovic, Kabayel and Itauma after second round winThirty minutes after Daniel Dubois had dismantled Fabio Wardley in less than two rounds on Saturday night, his promoter Frank Warren shook his head in slight awe as he described the intensity before the annihilation: “I went in the dressing room beforehand like I normally do and I couldn’t have a conversation with Daniel because he was so zoned in and focused. It showed when he got in the ring. He went out there on a seek-and-destroy mission.”Dubois resembled a much bigger and heavier version of a young Mike Tyson as, wearing black trunks and a black cape, he walked to the ring with intense purpose. There was not a flicker of emotion as he marched quickly towards Wardley for their WBO world title rematch. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by police

primary_source.headline: Sahil Wakode death: Protesting IIT Bombay students claim detention, use of excessive force by police
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Twenty-two IIT Bombay students, including eight who were allegedly detained twice in a single day, were picked up by the police from inside the campus on Sunday amid their ongoing protest demanding justice for deceased Sahil Wakode, student bodies said.The protesters and student collectives alleged that police used extreme force during the crackdown, accusing the cops of tearing their clothes, kicking and choking them. All detained students were taken to the Powai police station, they said.Police and IIT B authorities are yet to issue a detailed official statement regarding the scale of the detentions and the allegations of excessive force.Students have been protesting near the campus gates in the Powai area for a month, including a 15-day hunger strike, raising allegations of caste discrimination and institutional apathy surrounding the death of 22-year-old Sahil Wakode.IIT Bombay suicide: Sahil Wakode apologised for cheating in exam, sought second chance, say policeThe second-year B.Tech student was found dead in his hostel room on September 18 after allegedly being caught cheating during a mid-semester exam. Sunday marked one month since his alleged suicide, prompting students to plan a memorial and a ‘mashal juloos’ (torchlight procession).Student representatives alleged that police barged into the campus in large numbers in the morning. After an initial detention and brief release, students gathered at the protest site, alongside Wakode’s grieving parents to pay tribute, they said.Protesters alleged that the campus security and police subsequently dismantled the protest site and forcibly removed the participants. They also claimed that female students faced inappropriate touching and physical assault. A total of 22 students were detained, they said.The demonstrators also targeted the IIT Bombay administration over the deployment of police inside the campus, asking who authorised it.Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad and representatives of several Ambedkarite organisations subsequently reached the spot and staged a demonstration demanding an immediate meeting with the Chairperson of the Board of Governors and the Director.While officials from the Powai police station were not immediately available for comment, the institute authorities were yet to share their response to the detentions and allegations of excessive force.Wakode’s parents have been continuing their hunger strike at Azan Maidan in south Mumbai, demanding action and accountability from the institute administration.They have accused Professor Suryanarayana Doolla of harassment and caste-based discrimination. Earlier this month, the police questioned Doolla for nearly 10 hours in connection with the alleged suicide.

stories.primary_headline: Great Pottery Throw Down judge Keith Brymer Jones looks back: ‘Men like seeing me be emotional’

primary_source.headline: Great Pottery Throw Down judge Keith Brymer Jones looks back: ‘Men like seeing me be emotional’
primary_source.content: The potter and presenter on a tricky childhood, his religious calling for clay, and cross-dressing as AdeleBorn in London in 1965, Keith Brymer Jones is a potter, ceramic designer and TV judge. After a stint as lead singer of the punk band the Wigs, he became an apprentice at Harefield Pottery in London. He went on to set up his own company, and created pots and homewares for retailers including Conran, Habitat and Laura Ashley, before developing his signature Word range. He has been a judge on The Great Pottery Throw Down since it started in 2015. His new book, Firing Earth: An Unexpected History of Pots and Potters, is published on 22 October.This photo was taken in our family home in Finchley. Socks, shorts and a T-shirt was my usual outfit for scabbing around in the garden aged 11. I was a complete and utter square. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Man, 80, who died in light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond named
primary_source.content: Ian Haggis - pictured when he was younger - died when the light aircraft crashed near Loch Lomond He and a 16-year-old boy died when their plane came down near Loch Lomond. The teenager's identity has not been released. The pair had flown out from Glasgow Airport at 16:17 and stopped transmitting at 16:37, a few miles north east of the village of Drymen near Stirling. Emergency services were called to the scene of the crash at about 16:45 on Friday. Both of them were pronounced dead at the scene. Temporary airspace restrictions are currently in place over the area while the Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) carries out its inquiries.

stories.primary_headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending

primary_source.headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending
primary_source.content: In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable.It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Blunder in, abandon allies and court a dictator: it’s the Trump doctrine, now playing out in Myanmar | Steve Bloomfield

primary_source.headline: Blunder in, abandon allies and court a dictator: it’s the Trump doctrine, now playing out in Myanmar | Steve Bloomfield
primary_source.content: The US condemned the genocide and military rule there, but now that Trump craves its rare earths, that’s all changed. For democracy activists, that’s a disasterMarco Rubio was once adamant that the US had to do everything in its power to end what he described as the “ethnic cleansing” of the Rohingya in Myanmar. In a 2017 letter he signed along with 20 other US senators, Rubio called for “strong multilateral sanctions against specific senior Burmese military officials associated with the gross human rights abuses”. Those responsible for the atrocities should be prosecuted, he argued.In the years since, the Myanmar military’s crimes have only increased. What was then deemed ethnic cleansing of the Rohingya is now widely viewed, including by the US, as genocide. What little democracy existed in Myanmar was eradicated in 2021 when Aung San Suu Kyi was arrested and imprisoned and her party’s election victory overturned, and the military took full control. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina

primary_source.headline: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
primary_source.content: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors, of varying popularity, gazed disinterestedly at the scene. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara to feature special tableaux on Army, Navy, Air Force and more

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara to feature special tableaux on Army, Navy, Air Force and more
primary_source.content: Mysuru: With the countdown to the Dasara Jamboo Savari procession underway, more than 1,000 artists are busy preparing 53 tableaux at Bandipalya and the Karnataka Exhibition Authority grounds in Mysuru on Saturday.Seven special tableaux will showcase Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Tibetan settlements, Tulu Nadu, the Koragajja community and other themes. Another 18 tableaux by state government departments will depict initiatives and institutions, including the Bharat Jodo Yuva Sangha and the Tourism Department. Eleven tableaux representing the Central government will feature the Indian Army, Navy, Air Force and others. There will also be tableaux highlighting the specialities of 16 districts.Besides these, the procession will feature Ambari buses carrying sandalwood stars and sports personalities, an Air Force bus, Army and Navy bands, and Hallikar oxen.Activists demand volume caps on Mysuru Palace concerts to protect Dasara elephantsArtist S C Suresh was seen giving the finishing touches to tableaux showcasing the specialities of Hassan district along with his 10-member team. The tableaux will feature Booker Prize winner Banu Mushtaq, the Yettinahole Integrated Drinking Water Supply Project, a memorial for Dasara veteran Arjuna in the Yesalur range, Someshwara Temple and folk art forms such as Chikkimela and Togalu Gombeyaata.Artist Krishna Tiptur, who has won prizes five times, is working with his 22-member team on the tableaux representing Tumakuru district. The displays will feature nuclear scientist Raja Ramanna, who hailed from Tumakuru district, Devarayanadurga and the proposed Metro project. They will also highlight Tumakuru's status as an industrial, coconut and sports hub, including its international cricket and hockey stadiums.KSRTC Mysuru Rural Divisional Controller H T Veeresh was supervising work on the KSRTC tableaux, which will showcase buses ranging from the 'Banashankari' model of the 1970s to the latest models.Artist N Rajesh and his team were giving the finishing touches to tableaux representing Tulu Nadu, featuring Kambala, Kukke Subramanya Temple and other attractions.

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara: Final round of rehearsal begins for all 13 Dasara elephants

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara: Final round of rehearsal begins for all 13 Dasara elephants
primary_source.content: Mysuru: After 48 days of training, the final round of the last two days' of rehearsal began for all 13 Dasara Elephants infront of Mysuru Palace on Sunday morning.&nbsp;Flanked by Cauvery and Roopa, lead Elephant Prashantha, who has been finalised for carrying golden howdah, marched towards the podium.&nbsp;Chief Conservator of Forest Mysuru circle S S Ravishankar, DCF, Wildlife&nbsp;I B Prabhugowda, Mysuru city police commissioner Seema Latkar offered floral benediction as part of the rehearsal. On Wednesday Chief Minister D K Shivakumar will offer floral benediction to the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari which will be housed in golden howdah, mounted on Prashantha at the end of Dasara Jamboo Savari procession on Vijayadashami on October 21. This year, even Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Kerala who are expected to participate in the procession, are also likely to accompany CM D K Shivakumar on the podium, according to sources.Mysuru Dasara: 'Prashantha' to be lead elephant carrying golden howdah in Vijayadashami processionThe Police band led by band master B Manjunath, played even the national song-Vande Matharam for the first time along with the national Anthem during the floral benediction. Mounted cops&nbsp;also joined the rehearsal.&nbsp;Parade commander K N Suresh, Assistant Parade commander&nbsp;Sharanappa Sasanur&nbsp;accompanied the howdah Elephant.&nbsp;Prior to that, Abhimanyu marched as the&nbsp;Nishaane Elephant leading the procession at the forefront. Gopi followed him as the Nauphath Elephant. Mahendra and Lakshmi; Srirama, Chithra and Sugreeva; Srikanta and Ekalavya marched as Saalanes in three batches.&nbsp;Veteran Abhimanyu who carried golden howdah for six years till last year, has been relieved from this prime duty this year as he has turned 60 years of age. Hence Prashantha, Mahendra, Dhananjaya, Ekalavya and Sugreeva were trained to carry the weight equivalent to golden howdah. After the completion of their training on Tuesday, Prashantha was finalised on Wednesday to carry golden howdah in the procession.&nbsp;Dasara elephants, horses acquainted with cannon fire shotsThe first batch of nine Dasara elephants arrived at the Aranya Bhavan in Mysuru after a grand Gajapayana event at Veeranahosahalli in Hunsur taluk on August 26. They were accorded a grand traditional welcome on the Palace premises on August 28 and have been housed there since then. Their weight was checked, and they are being treated to a special nutritious diet to maintain their strength and build stamina for the big day, from August 30. Their training began on August 30. They were familiarised with the crowd, and the procession route from Palace to Government Ayurveda college circle till September 4. From September 5, they were familiarised with the entire procession route till Bannimantap ground. Training to carry weight began on September 6. Elephants Sugreeva, Roopa and Chaithra arrived in the second batch on September 13. Training to carry wooden howdah began on September 25. They were acquainted with cannon fire shots from brass barrels on October 7, 9 and 12, as 21 Cannon shots will be fired during floral benediction to Goddess at the end of procession on Vijayadashami.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: Suspects hunted after police officer injured in shooting

primary_source.headline: Suspects hunted after police officer injured in shooting
primary_source.content: The officer was shot after approaching two people in Angel Row, Nottingham Nottinghamshire Police said the officer had approached two suspects in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday. The officer is in a stable condition in hospital, where he is receiving treatment for a wound to his foot, the force added. Detectives said a man and a woman had fled the scene and that a firearm, which could be seen within the cordon, had been found. Angel Row is currently closed and a large police scene remains in place. Police cars are parked along the road, which is lined by fast food stores and shops, and orange traffic cones have been laid out alongside items left on the road.

The officer is in a stable condition in hospital, where he is receiving treatment for a wound to his foot, the force added. Detectives said a man and a woman had fled the scene and that a firearm, which could be seen within the cordon, had been found. Angel Row is currently closed and a large police scene remains in place. Police cars are parked along the road, which is lined by fast food stores and shops, and orange traffic cones have been laid out alongside items left on the road.

stories.primary_headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction

primary_source.headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: While Keralam suffers acute shortage of construction materials owing to the restriction imposed by Tamil Nadu government in transporting construction materials, huge quantities of construction materials are remaining unutilised in the rivers and dams in the state. According to a data presented by the state government in the assembly, after the 2018-19 floods it was evaluated that 43 of the 44 rivers in Keralam alone had a sand and silt deposit of&nbsp; 30.17 million cubic metre that could be removed. The capacity of 15 of the 81 dams in the state alone came down by an average of 13.8 percent owing to the silt accumulation. Huge sand deposits in Kerala rivers remain untapped Studies have found that the carrying capacity of Vebanad lake, the largest lake in Keralam, came down by up to 85 percent owing to reasons like silt deposit as well as encroachments. The silt accumulation in the water bodies, which reduced the water holding capacity, has been found to be a reason for flash floods in the state. Keralam, which requires up to 30 million metric tonnes of sand annually, has been highly dependent on Tamil Nadu for rocks to sand. Hence the restriction by the neighbouring state has led to an acute scarcity in Keralam, which already led to almost three times cost escalation. Major infrastructure projects like the ongoing expansion of Vizhinjam international seaport and national highway were reportedly feeling the heat. Desilting of the water bodies is hence considered to have multiple benefits ranging from addressing construction material shortage to flood mitigation. Tamil Nadu bans transportation of rough stones to other states; Kerala seeks review The state government was forced to impose a ban on river sand mining in 2016 in view of the massive unregulated sand mining which even diverted the direction of flow of rivers at many places. Hence, the state has been depending on manufactured sand for construction. The stringent regulations for quarries have also&nbsp; led to the number of quarries coming down around 220 from 3800 ten years back, according to the Keralam Mining and Crushing Owners Association. Even as the state government initiated steps for desilting at a couple of dams like the Mangalam dam in Palakkad and introduced stringent norms for regulated river sand mining following the 2018-19 floods, those steps went into troubled waters&nbsp; owing to allegations of over exploitation and ecological concerns. Industry sources said that since the chances of Tamil Nadu easing the restrictions was remote, the state government should proactively take steps to address the crisis.&nbsp; Natural river sand offers a better construction quality than manufactured sand. Hence the government should take steps for regulated desilting and river sand mining," said Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India general convener general. However, environmental expert V Subashchandrabose points out that even as scientific desilting and river sand mining could be allowed, the state should popularise alternative&nbsp; construction methods that could reduce the dependence on natural resources.

stories.primary_headline: Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran's exit notice row

primary_source.headline: Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran's exit notice row
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Actor-filmmaker Aamir Khan met Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray at his residence in Mumbai on Sunday.The details of the meeting were not immediately known.The meeting comes days after Aamir Khan's nephew and actor Imran Khan was served a notice by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28. Imran had reportedly participated in the October 10 protests at August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.The 43-year-old Imran Khan is a US citizen and an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.'Leave India': Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against 'illegal, bad in law' notice by Mumbai police, FRRO issues him show-cause noticeHe has challenged the notice in the Bombay High Court, which is expected to hear the matter this week. The plea is expected to be mentioned for an urgent hearing before a division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna.“The notice has been issued without disclosing any reasons, supporting material, or specific statutory contravention. It was issued without inquiry, a show-cause notice, or any opportunity for the Petitioner (Khan) to respond to the alleged violations,” the plea stated.The FRRO issued the notice under Sections 7 and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, directing Imran Khan to leave India by October 28, 2026.

stories.primary_headline: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children a priority, says health secretary

primary_source.headline: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children a priority, says health secretary
primary_source.content: No patient should be treated in a corridor, Yvette Cooper says Yvette Cooper told the BBC there would be new standards for caring for children in A&E in England, with figures collected on corridor care by age for the first time. She was speaking on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg where the programme highlighted the case of two-year-old Finlay Roberts who died in a hospital corridor in 2024. The health secretary has announced £140m to improve urgent care in England ahead of what she said would be a "more difficult" winter than usual. The government has already pledged to end corridor care for all patients by the end of this parliament, and now Cooper has said eradicating it for children would be prioritised. Corridor care refers to patients receiving treatment or waiting in corridors, waiting rooms or other hospital areas due to a lack of appropriate space.

stories.primary_headline: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting

primary_source.headline: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
primary_source.content: A vandalised shopfront in Paris in the aftermath of protests Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday as some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for protests that were largely peaceful. They were demonstrating against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools. Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings. Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas. In Paris, protesters clashed with riot police, who turned tear gas and water cannon on the crowds. During the day, some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles. At least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups.

stories.primary_headline: How to make the perfect poires belle Hélène – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect …

primary_source.headline: How to make the perfect poires belle Hélène – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect …
primary_source.content: Cool, juicy pears, cold ice-cream, hot chocolate sauce and a crunchy garnish – the perfect puddingIt’s always slightly embarrassing to realise that you’ve missed a pop culture reference, even if it’s 162 years old, so I won’t dwell on the fact that until last week I was unaware of the existence of Offenbach’s 1864 operetta about Helen of Troy, La Belle Hélène, after which today’s dish is named. In any case, the great French chef Escoffier was so moved by it, or perhaps by its popularity among Parisian diners, to name this simple dessert of vanilla-scented poached pears topped with hot chocolate sauce after the work’s heroine, played by the comely Hortense Schneider.Though other homages (he includes no fewer than five dishes with that name in his 1907 Guide Culinaire, none of which involve pears) may, like the music, have faded from public consciousness, this particular pairing, if you’ll forgive the pun, has stood the test of time. As Nigel Slater observes in Tender: Volume 2, “The marriage of pears and chocolate is extraordinary. It is as if they were made for each other.” This, I think, is the duo at its “most sumptuous”. In any case, the great French chef Escoffier was so moved by it, or perhaps by its popularity among Parisian diners, to name this simple dessert of vanilla-scented poached pears topped with hot chocolate sauce after the work’s heroine, played by the comely Hortense Schneider.Though other homages (he includes no fewer than five dishes with that name in his 1907 Guide Culinaire, none of which involve pears) may, like the music, have faded from public consciousness, this particular pairing, if you’ll forgive the pun, has stood the test of time. As Nigel Slater observes in Tender: Volume 2, “The marriage of pears and chocolate is extraordinary. It is as if they were made for each other.” This, I think, is the duo at its “most sumptuous”. Continue reading...
