stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara airshow: Surya Kiran's dazzling display cut short by rain

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara airshow: Surya Kiran's dazzling display cut short by rain
primary_source.content: Mysuru: The Suryakiran Aerobatic Team (SKAT) of the Indian Air Force, enthralled the jam-packed crowd at Bannimantap ground with their spectacular aerial display during Dasara Airshow in Mysuru on Sunday morning. However, due to rain and inclement weather conditions, the air warriors could only perform three horizontal manoeuvres, including the arrow manoeuvre with nine Hawk Mk 132 aircraft, in the blue sky canvas of Mysuru. The display was complemented by saffron, white and green smoke trails. The team, known for its precision, coordination, synchronisation, discipline and teamwork, performed with all the aircraft operating as a cohesive unit.Mysuru Dasara to feature special tableaux on Army, Navy, Air Force and moreMysuru: Farmers' Dasara turns into platform to inspire community towards independent livelihood, women empowermentThe people who had gathered after the gates of the ground opened at 9 am could witness the show for about 10 minutes from 11.20 am. They were disappointed as the team could not continue the show in view of the safety of pilots and the aircraft due to weather conditions. However, people returned with hope, as the show will be held on Monday too. On Monday, the Surya Kiran team will be flying all the nine aircraft, manufactured under licence by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL). They plan to showcase a series of intricate aerobatic manoeuvres, including both horizontal and vertical ones. Signature manoeuvres such as loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and the DNA manoeuvres can also be witnessed.Set up in 1996, the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team has a legacy of representing the Indian Air Force and the nation at air shows and public events across India and abroad. With over 800 displays to its credit, the team is inspiring generations of aviation enthusiasts and young Indians to consider a career in the Indian Air Force.  The display forms part of the team’s continued endeavour to bring the Indian Air Force closer to the people of the country. The show has been an opportunity for people to witness the synergy between man and machine, where every manoeuvre reflects the dedication, skill and teamwork that define the Indian Air Force.

stories.primary_headline: A California town’s beaches are washing away. Can its residents turn the tide?

primary_source.headline: A California town’s beaches are washing away. Can its residents turn the tide?
primary_source.content: Rapid coastal erosion threatens coastal homes and economies, and as Super El Niño rounds the corner, a town is reckoning with the reality of climate crisisSan Clemente is one of southern California’s most picture-perfect beach towns – a capital of American surf culture since the 1950s. In two years, 2028 Olympic surfers will compete at Lower Trestles, a world-class surfing beach.But the town’s longtime cultural and economic driver, its beaches, are now under threat. As pounding waves driven by late-summer storms in the Pacific devour chunks of the California coastline, some of San Clemente’s beaches are growing narrower, the sand increasingly eaten away. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage

primary_source.headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: Keralam Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan on Sunday expressed dissatisfaction with the Devaswom Board's preparations for the upcoming annual Sabarimala pilgrimage season.The minister's remarks came a day after he and Chief Minister V D Satheesan visited the various places associated with the Sabarimala pilgrimage to review preparations and facilities for the upcoming season.After the review meeting, the CM said that all arrangements related to temple rituals and prasadam were under the control of the Devaswom Board, and its president has assured that there will be no shortage of prasadam or other facilities at the shrine.On Sunday, Muraleedharan told a TV channel that repair and renovation of the plant manufacturing the 'aravana payasam' prasadam has not been completed yet.He also said that there was an apparent lack of coordination between the Board and the police with regard to crowd control.BJP steps up attack on Keralam govt over Sabarimala arrangementsThe minister said that his two main concerns were regulating the large number of devotees who arrived for the pilgrimage and ensuring a sufficient supply of 'appam' and 'aravana' for the pilgrims.'Aravana' -- a thick, sweet dessert made from red rice, jaggery, ghee, cardamom powder, and ginger powder -- and 'appam' -- a traditional sweet rice cake/fritter made with ingredients like rice and jaggery -- are the two primary 'prasadam' at the Lord Ayyappa shrine at Sabarimala."I am not completely satisfied with the steps being taken to ensure the prasadam sufficiency. The contract for the rice has not yet been finalised by the Board. I have been told that the repair and renovation of the plant will be completed by November 5 and production will be started," Muraleedharan said.He said that he has told the Board to give specific attention to these issues.The minister said that 29,000 devotees reached the shrine on Saturday ahead of the commencement of the 'Thula masam' puja on Sunday and currently there were two lakh aravana in stock."I have told the Board to take extra care regarding the matter up to October 22 (when the shrine will close again). After that, they have to ensure things are much better," he said.The Sabarimala shrine will be open for five days during the 'Thula masam' -- the third month in the traditional Malayalam calendar -- from October 18 to October 22.Muraleedharan also said that there was a delay in the completion of temple maintenance works."The government is doing all that has to be done," he added.The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple will open on November 17 for the 41-day Mandalam pilgrimage season.

stories.primary_headline: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

primary_source.headline: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
primary_source.content: The BBC’s Quentin Sommerville joins officers at Cook County as they carry out an early morning raid The few grains of fentanyl sit in the silver foil as a straw, held between Mike's lips, hovers above, with a cigarette lighter below. The 48-year-old army veteran is crouched low in an alleyway in Columbus, Ohio's Linden neighbourhood. "This drug will damn near make you do anything, unfortunately," he says. The hit he's smoking cost three or four dollars. "You can snort too much and you can't take it back. Kind of like a gunshot. Can't call the bullet back," he says. He burns the foil and inhales. stories.primary_headline: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat

primary_source.headline: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
primary_source.content: What stands out is the 50m swimming pool along the deck, with a cluster of waterslides at one end. After sitting idle for months at a maintenance facility, it relocated in early July to waters off a strip of coastline known as the Kalma Peninsula. This is close to Wonsan, a seaside resort with a sprawling villa used by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his family. It was not the only large vessel on the move. A handful of others were also repeatedly seen near Kim's villa, in satellite images analysed by the BBC. The vessels are widely believed to be used by Kim and his family. Former North Korean officials, defectors and experts say it would be difficult for anyone unconnected to the regime's leadership to own or freely use vessels of this size. "In winter, they would keep them at the shipyard. When summer came, they would bring them out and move them to Kim Jong Un's villa or towards Kalma, and use them for swimming and recreation," says Ri Jong Ho.

stories.primary_headline: Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team to stage aerial show in Mysuru on Oct 18 and 19

primary_source.headline: Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team to stage aerial show in Mysuru on Oct 18 and 19
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: The Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team (SKAT) of the Indian Air Force, renowned for its precision, discipline and teamwork, is set to enthral the people of Mysuru with a spectacular aerial display on October 18 and 19 during the Dasara.&nbsp;Flying nine Hawk Mk 132 aircraft, manufactured under licence by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), the team will showcase a series of intricate aerobatic manoeuvres that promise to leave spectators spellbound. Signature manoeuvres such as loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and the iconic DNA manoeuvre will demonstrate exceptional precision, coordination and synchronisation. Performed in close formation, with nine aircraft operating as one cohesive unit, the display will be complemented by vibrant saffron, white and green smoke trails, adding to the spectacle in the skies over Mysuru.Established in 1996, the SKAT has a proud legacy of representing the Indian Air Force and the nation at air shows and public events across India and abroad. With over 850 displays to its credit, the team has become a symbol of the Service’s flying excellence, discipline and professionalism, inspiring generations of aviation enthusiasts and young Indians. Every display is the culmination of extensive training, meticulous planning and complete trust among the pilots and the support team.Mysuru, celebrated for its magnificent palaces, architectural splendour and rich cultural heritage, provides a distinguished setting for this aerial showcase. The display will offer the people of the city an opportunity to witness the remarkable synergy between man and machine, where every manoeuvre reflects the dedication, skill and teamwork that define the Indian Air Force.The display forms part of the SKAT’s continued endeavour to bring the Indian Air Force closer to the people of the country. Through its spectacular aerial performances, the team provides the public with an opportunity to witness the skill, precision and professionalism of the Service, while inspiring young Indians to aspire to excellence and consider a career in the Indian Air Force.The SKAT looks forward to enthralling the people of Mysuru with its signature aerial manoeuvres and bringing a memorable display of precision and aerial excellence to the city.Squadron Leader Vikram of the SKAT spoke to DH on the sidelines of the press conference in Bengaluru on Saturday:&nbsp;Excerpts:Q) What special manoeuvres have you planned for the display? Are they new?A) One of the special highlights of our Mysuru display will be a series of flybys by all nine aircraft in formations similar to the various monuments around this historic city. We invite everyone to look out for this special formation during the display. Along with this special tribute, we will bring the thrill and excitement of our signature aerobatic manoeuvres to the skies of Mysuru, including loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and our iconic DNA manoeuvre. Through these manoeuvres, performed with precision and synchronisation by all nine aircraft, we hope to thrill the people of Mysuru and give them an unforgettable experience.Q) Have you customised this particular show for Karnataka and the special occasion?A) We are delighted to be back in Mysuru and to perform before the people of Karnataka. We will be presenting a special display that connects with the local heritage and cultural identity of this region. Through this performance, we hope to celebrate the rich cultural heritage of Mysuru and Karnataka, connect meaningfully with the people of this beautiful city, and inspire the youth of our country to aspire to join the Indian Air Force and serve the nation.&nbsp;The display is also dedicated to the spirit of the Indian Air Force as it celebrates 94 years of service to the nation, reflecting our shared pride and commitment to the country.

primary_source.headline: Plaque telling story of African-Caribbean prisoners in Britain stolen within days
primary_source.content: Descendants say theft from Portchester Castle reflects racism that has haunted ‘generation after generation’The theft of a plaque in Hampshire that told the little-known story of African-Caribbean prisoners in 18th-century Britain reflects the enduring racism that has fuelled centuries of atrocities against Black and Indigenous Caribbean people, their descendants say.Ronald Raymond McDonald, a professional drummer, was part of a delegation that travelled from Belize and elsewhere to Portchester Castle near Portsmouth last week to honour their ancestors: 2,500 men, women and children transported to Britain as prisoners of war in 1796. stories.primary_headline: 'Couldn't prevent regime change within Shiv Sena': Maharashtra CM Fadnavis takes dig at Uddhav Thackeray

primary_source.headline: 'Couldn't prevent regime change within Shiv Sena': Maharashtra CM Fadnavis takes dig at Uddhav Thackeray
primary_source.content: Mumbai: A day after Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray backed the ‘regime change’ call, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday took a dig at him saying he could not prevent a regime change in his own party. Fadnavis was referring to the June-July 2022 rebellion in the Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde — who toppled Thackeray’s Maha Vikas Aghadi government with the help of BJP to become the Chief Minister. Slamming Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Thackeray on Saturday said: “Yes we are ready for a regime change…particularly If right to express ourselves through vote and right to protest is being taken away then we have to change regime.”Uddhav Thackeray backs Prashant Bhushan's regime change call, cites curbs on voting, protest rightsHowever, Fadnavis, on Sunday hit back at Thackeray, a former ally, who is now a key leader of the Congress-led INDIA opposition bloc. "Firstly, if Uddhav Thackeray could not prevent a 'regime change' within the Shiv Sena itself, I fail to understand what other 'regime change' he is referring to,” said Fadnavis, a senior BJP leader. "When his party abandoned Hindutva and discarded the ideals of the ‘Hindu Hriday Samrat' and Shiv Sena supremo Balasaheb Thackeray, it caused such an upheaval within his own ranks that those who wished to remain true to Balasaheb’s vision formed the 'real' Shiv Sena,” said Fadnavis. “My clear message is — stop challenging the Constitution of India. Decisions here will be made in Parliament, in accordance with the Constitution—not on the streets,” he said, adding: “If you want a regime change, you have to contest polls, win the hearts of the people, and secure a mandate.”

primary_source.headline: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile
primary_source.content: Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years agoA few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”.Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: The upside of anger: can fury be one of the deepest forms of human compassion? | Making sense of it

primary_source.headline: The upside of anger: can fury be one of the deepest forms of human compassion? | Making sense of it
primary_source.content: Imagine anger as a sign not of moral failure or justified outrage but the desire to care for anotherMaking sense of it is a column about spirituality and how it can be used to navigate everyday lifeAnger is an emotion we are taught to manage, control and suppress. But what if anger is, as poet David Whyte says, one of the deepest possible forms of compassion available to humankind?Philosophers and theologians have long distinguished between virtuous and non-virtuous anger. Aristotle defined anger as “a desire, accompanied by pain, for apparent retribution, aroused by an apparent, undeserved slighting against oneself or those connected to oneself”. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: India's education system is an 'exclusion' plan keeping youth out, alleges Rahul Gandhi

primary_source.headline: India's education system is an 'exclusion' plan keeping youth out, alleges Rahul Gandhi
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday criticised the education system in India, calling it an "exclusion system" that is designed to keep millions of youth out.His remarks came during an interaction he had with students recently, a video of which was posted on his social media handles.Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers"If you don’t have money, power, or don't speak English, the system will push you out without a second thought. You can’t call this an education system. It’s an exclusion system - designed to keep millions of Indian youth out," he said.He said what the current system is doing is certifying people and creating a "fake idea of merit".&nbsp;His comments came as a student said the National Education Policy is exclusionary with most of the students not being able to pursue studies in regular colleges owing to the Common University Entrance Test.

stories.primary_headline: ‘This is horrifying. This is madness’: the row over competitive yoga

primary_source.headline: ‘This is horrifying. This is madness’: the row over competitive yoga
primary_source.content: Some yogis welcome the idea of competition – for others, it is anathema. Will those keen for yoga to become an Olympic sport win the argument?Vaishnavi Saravanakumar describes herself on Instagram as “India’s rubber band girl”. In a typical video post, dressed in a rhinestone-studded crimson catsuit and accompanied by a Bollywood-rap anthem, she demonstrates an improbable feat. From standing, she snakes into a deep back bend, curls her head and shoulders up under her tiger-striped calves, and finishes beaming to camera with ankles crossed under her chin. This is yoga as we have seldom seen it before.Earlier this year, the Indian government announced that it will push for yogasana’s inclusion in the Olympics, ahead of the country’s bid to host the 2036 Games. The news came the week before the inaugural World Yogasana Championship, held in Ahmedabad in June, at which Saravanakumar, a gold medallist, was one of 522 yogis competing. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: BJP's Yediyurappa alleges CM Shivakumar part of plot to dethrone Siddaramaiah

primary_source.headline: BJP's Yediyurappa alleges CM Shivakumar part of plot to dethrone Siddaramaiah
primary_source.content: Davanagere: BJP Parliamentary Board member and former Chief Minister B S Yediyurappa charged that many leaders including Chief Minister D K Shivakumar hatched a conspiracy to dethrone Siddaramaiah from the post of chief minister.Addressing media persons, here on Sunday, he stated that tolerance of Siddaramaiah is difficult to understand, but noted that the truth will soon come to light. He remarked that a systematic plot was executed to remove Siddaramaiah from the top post and create chaos in the state. D K Shivakumar is intoxicated by power and shows no willingness to correct his mistakes.HDK, JD(S) workers stage protest outside DGP office, demand immediate arrest of Rakesh Shetty over 'sting op' videosResponding to a question, he said, the state government is oblivious to the drought situation and the hardships faced by the people and farmers. It is displaying the height of irresponsibility at every turn. Despite having a vast majority, the Congress is running a 'Tughlaq-style' (arbitrary and chaotic) administration. The people must teach them a fitting lesson in the next election.Meanwhile, Chitradurga MP Govind Karjol urged that those in politics should serve as role models for society rather than acting like 'demons.' He called for an end to such low-level politics and demanded strict legal action against those who engage in despicable acts like 'sting operations.'

stories.primary_headline: Unacceptable, says Chirag on Imran Khan’s protest

primary_source.headline: Unacceptable, says Chirag on Imran Khan’s protest
primary_source.content: Patna: Union Minister Chirag Paswan has slammed actor Imran Khan for protesting in India against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and called Khan’s act as “an attempt to create anarchy, backed by foreign powers.”Paswan, who made his film debut in 2011 opposite Kangana Ranaut in the movie Miley Naa Miley Hum, said, “I like the work of Imran Khan. I rate him high as an actor. But foreign nationals like Imran Khan should not have protested in India. I am not against peaceful protests by Indians. But if a foreign national protests or holds demonstrations, then it’s absolutely unacceptable,” said Paswan, backing the Indian Government’s decision asking Imran, nephew of Aamir Khan, to leave India this month itself.'Leave India': Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against 'illegal, bad in law' notice by Mumbai police, FRRO issues him show-cause noticeThe LJP (R) president, who is also a Lok Sabha member from Bihar’s Hajipur was speaking to mediamen here on Sunday about actor Imran Khan who is an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder. “Why should someone, who is not an Indian citizen, get involved in the internal affairs of our country. As part of the Indian Government, I am concerned over attempts being made to create anarchy in India with the support of foreign powers,” said Paswan, who himself made an unsuccessful bid in Bollywood before joining the hurly burly of Indian politics after his debut movie ‘Miley Naa Miley Hum’ sank like a ‘Titanic’ at the box-office.Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers Chirag also slammed Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for going ahead with his Goa rally. “See the difference. On the one hand, Union Home Minister Amit Shah cancelled his engagements in view of the Kolkata tragedy. On the other hand, we have Rahul Gandhi for whom only politics matters. This is the contrast,” said Chirag, while slamming the Congress leader.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers

primary_source.headline: Rahul Gandhi joins Congress' 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Goa; walks 2 km with party workers
primary_source.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday participated in the party's 'Goy Rakhon Yatra' in Margao, walking two kilometres alongside party workers and leaders.Gandhi arrived at Dabolim airport in the afternoon to join the mass outreach programme. He is scheduled to address a public gathering at the Margao Cricket Club (MCC) ground later in the day.Among those who accompanied him during the yatra were AICC Goa desk in-charge Manikrao Thakare, co-in-charge Dr Anjali Nimbalkar, Leader of Opposition Yuri Alemao and Goa Pradesh Congress Committee president Girish Chodankar.The 27-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', led by Alemao and Chodankar, began on September 22 and concluded on Sunday. The campaign covered all 40 Assembly constituencies in Goa as the Congress seeks to strengthen its grassroots network ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Rahul Gandhi to address Goa rally as Congress wraps up 28-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra'The party described the 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', which translates to a campaign to protect Goa, as a movement to safeguard the state's land, environment, cultural heritage and identity.Throughout the campaign, the Congress highlighted concerns over land conversion, alleged land grabbing, unemployment, corruption and public safety, while emphasising the need to preserve Goa's distinct social and cultural identity.The yatra also aimed to engage with local communities and bring development-related issues to the forefront of political discussions.With the 2027 Goa Assembly elections approaching, the Congress is seeking to expand its grassroots presence and mobilise support across constituencies, including those currently represented by the ruling BJP.

stories.primary_headline: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion

primary_source.headline: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion
primary_source.content: Watch: Polanski says practical application of Zionism is racist The Green leader told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, it would be party policy until 2028. The motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month, described Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population". He came under criticism for not voting on the motion which was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 - a small fraction of the party's 230,000 members - in Brighton earlier this month. The motion also asserted the party's backing for "a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine", a full arms embargo on Israel and a commitment to Palestinian liberation. Asked if he would now step in as leader to overturn it, Polanski said: "I'm not going to try to overturn it.

stories.primary_headline: 'Mujhe kidnap hi kar liya tha': Reality TV star Akanksha Choudhary narrates 'deeply disturbing' incident; accuses event organisers of misconduct

primary_source.headline: 'Mujhe kidnap hi kar liya tha': Reality TV star Akanksha Choudhary narrates 'deeply disturbing' incident; accuses event organisers of misconduct
primary_source.content: Reality TV star Akanksha Choudhary, who was recently seen in Lock Upp 2, has narrated her ordeal, making serious allegations against the Navratri event organisers in Pune.Taking to her Instagram Stories, Choudhary accused the organisers of mismanagement, non-payment of her dues, and "kidnapping" her.The event, which was held at Pedkar Grounds in Pune, was organised by three members of the management team, who, according to Choudhary, were 18 years old.&nbsp;In a series of Instagram Stories, Choudhary narrated her ordeal of how she made to wait till 10.30 since no one from the management team came to pick her up for the event and that she had to reach the event venue by herself.She then accused the organisers of scamming her, along with other artists, and not clearing their dues.Choudhary further added that the situation became even more uncomfortable when she was made to sit in a car and taken inside the venue ground.Screengrab of Akanksha Choudhary's Instagram Story.She claimed that the car was stopped right in front of the audience despite her telling the organisers that she cannot enter the venue without her team as she does not feel safe.She further alleged all her pleas went unheard and the young organisers kept laughing at her."Zabardasti gaadi mein bitakar, ground mein chhod diya, and in front of the audience they stopped. Main chilla rahi hoon ki main andar nahi ja sakti, meri team nahi hai mere saath. It is not safe, aur yeh bacche hass rahe hain, meri baat nahi sun rahe hain. Itna stupid management. Chor hain yeh ekdum, sabka payment le liya, use kar liya," Choudhary said.Screengrab of Akanksha Choudhary's Instagram Story.She further went on to call the incident a kidnapping-like situation, and added, "Mujhe kidnap hi kar liya tha sort of, jab maine thappad maari unko, tab rukhe woh. Unpe case sab karungi, chhodungi nahi main."In the following Instagram Stories, Choudhary also claimed that she, along with her team members, were subjected to intimation, threats and mental harassment, from the organisers who claimed that they belong to influential families and that they will handle the matter in their "own way".Calling the incident "deeply disturbing", Choudhary threatened legal action against those involved.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy

primary_source.headline: ‘Medieval romance overflowed with sexually active fairies’: the surprisingly long roots of romantasy
primary_source.content: Critics mock it as raunchy trash – but this enchanting genre is much older, and wilder, than you might imagineThere’s a popular genre, filled with beautiful, human-sized fairies having sex with humans (often quite violent sex, but the people reading it seem to enjoy it). Word is that it’s badly written and unashamedly escapist – all golden, glittering palaces, wild adventure and, of course, gorgeous fairies. It’s certainly popular – plenty of the stories have been translated into numerous languages, spreading across continents. Serious commentators are sure it spells bad news: at best, it’s just a load of trash; at worst, it’s actively leading people astray. Most damningly of all, women produce and consume it. Welcome to the 12th century, where fairy romance is all the rage. Sound familiar?The romantasy that fills our shelves and bestseller lists – from Sarah J Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses to Callie Hart’s Quicksilver – is not a new genre, but part of a centuries-old heritage. You only need to look at the medieval predecessors of the modern romantasy novel to understand why it’s enjoyed by millions and why, even after hundreds of years, fairy romance has such power over us – and why there are still those who want to diminish and dismiss it. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Getaway cars, affairs, Dubai fugitives: Trump’s pick Ken Paxton brings baggage to Senate race in Texas

primary_source.headline: Getaway cars, affairs, Dubai fugitives: Trump’s pick Ken Paxton brings baggage to Senate race in Texas
primary_source.content: The Republican state attorney general appears uniquely ill-chosen as a candidate – but he is a political survivor who could yet frustrate Democratic dreamsDepending how you look at the situation, it is either predictable that Ken Paxton, Texas’s attorney general and Republican candidate for US Senate, is struggling in the polls – or impressive that he is not doing worse. Beloved by hardcore Maga voters and regarded with skepticism by the broader voting public, Paxton is also puzzlingly bland. Recently, Donald Trump told a crowd of supporters that the 63-year-old Paxton “may not dress right, he may not talk exactly perfectly, and he may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen”. The president was endorsing him.Yet it is Paxton’s ability to attract – and somehow scrape through – scandal that makes him a less charismatic, perhaps, but still kindred spirit of “Teflon Don”: nothing sticks. He has survived state prosecution (on securities-related charges that he settled without admitting guilt), impeachment by the Republican-led Texas legislature (on abuse-of-office charges of which he was later acquitted), and so many controversies that it can be difficult to pin down the most outrageous. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music

primary_source.headline: Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music
primary_source.content: Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowdsFor the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture

primary_source.headline: ‘Shakespeare was a Black woman’: the playwright’s under-recognized connection to Black culture
primary_source.content: A new Washington DC exhibition examines how Toni Morrison, Maya Angelou and more used the Bard’s work to help tell their own stories“William Shakespeare was a black woman.” In 1985, Maya Angelou spoke these words as part of a keynote speech at a convention in Cedar Rapids, Iowa.There, she spoke of the role poetry played in her transition from muteness as a child and how she fantasized herself triumphantly delivering Portia’s speech from William Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice in front of her entire community at church. Though she never got the chance to perform that rendition, Angelou acknowledged her desire to deliver that rendition as part of a lifelong kinship with Shakespeare, a connection she continued to seek out throughout her life whenever she needed heartening or solace. In her eyes, Shakespeare wrote his emotionally desolate Sonnet 29 “for” her; how else could he have so aptly described the harsh realities of the Black feminine condition? Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: More peas, please! 17 delicious ways to devour Britain’s most brilliant vegetable
primary_source.content: They’re healthy, versatile, sustainable and available. Yet pea consumption in the UK is at a 50-year low. Here are the curries, dips, pasta dishes and even cakes that could turn all that aroundIt’s not good news for the pea farmers: pea consumption in the UK has fallen to a 50-year low. According to data from Defra, the average Briton ate just 37g of peas per week in 2025, down from 144g per week in 1975.Though a classic British staple, peas are not for everybody. Apparently only 22% of gen Z associate peas with Britain at all (which is patently ridiculous: 90% of the peas we consume in the UK are grown here, while we produce about 160,000 tonnes for freezing alone each year). primary_source.headline: ‘I drunkenly sing Wonderwall off-key and awfully’: Rebecca Ferguson’s honest playlist
primary_source.content:
The singer-songwriter gets a lift from U2 and likes to reminisce to Bette Midler, but which cheesy Euro banger does she secretly like?The first song I fell in love with
 
 When I was five or six, my mum wouldn’t let me listen to anything other than Christian gospel. Her friend Jane felt sorry for me and brought me a cassette with Whitney Houston on one side and Cher on the other. My ears couldn’t believe what they were hearing. I Will Always Love You made me think: This is what I’m going to do.The first single I bought
 
 So Young by the Corrs, from Sainsbury’s in Walton Village in Liverpool. I couldn’t really afford music as a kid, so buying a record was a big deal. I’d heard the Corrs on the radio, liked their voices and thought: I’m buying this. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool

primary_source.headline: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool
primary_source.content: It will be a tense time for club’s president despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have comeThe first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 against Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much.But then, he never enjoys it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous,” he says. “It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious. I suffer a lot. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: ‘We hang on to summer a little longer here’: five of the best places for autumn sun in Europe and Turkey

primary_source.headline: ‘We hang on to summer a little longer here’: five of the best places for autumn sun in Europe and Turkey
primary_source.content: If you’re looking for a last blast of summer, these sunny resorts offer quiet beaches but enough life to stave off the end-of-season bluesA Kalkan sunset is always a beautiful thing – the horseshoe-shaped bay deepening to azure blue against an apricot-rose sky – but, in October, when the light is low and the sun drops early, it’s almost transcendentally lovely. In some Turkish resorts, you’d be sitting watching it surrounded by quiet streets, half-empty bars and that melancholic sense that another season is over. In Kalkan, it still feels like summer; the harbourfront restaurants throng with visitors, the day gulets (wooden boats) still putter in and out of the bay and you don’t have to wait an hour to get a taxi back to your villa. stories.primary_headline: ‘How do we welcome the stranger, with humanity or anger?’ The forgotten Germans who found refuge in Ireland

primary_source.headline: ‘How do we welcome the stranger, with humanity or anger?’ The forgotten Germans who found refuge in Ireland
primary_source.content: A new play revisits the story of Ireland’s 18th-century German refugees, whose experience of prejudice and exclusion resonates with today’s debates over immigrationIn the early 18th century, a few thousand Germans fled religious persecution and near starvation in their homeland and ended up in remote rural Irish villages. The Irish Palatines, as they were known, were poor, conservative homesteaders who couldn’t speak the language and were the object of suspicion and violence – precursors to the displaced Syrians or Afghans of the past decade.Their story is told in Refuge, a co-production between Staatstheater Mainz and the Irish company Fishamble. Part love story, part social commentary, it is performed by a mixed cast, mainly in English but with some German interludes. Continue reading...

The Irish Palatines, as they were known, were poor, conservative homesteaders who couldn’t speak the language and were the object of suspicion and violence – precursors to the displaced Syrians or Afghans of the past decade.Their story is told in Refuge, a co-production between Staatstheater Mainz and the Irish company Fishamble. Part love story, part social commentary, it is performed by a mixed cast, mainly in English but with some German interludes. Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: My longterm boyfriend died last year. Is it too soon to date someone new? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
primary_source.content: Only you can know when you are ready, but a year is not long to process grief, and you seem to have doubts about this manMy longterm boyfriend died of cancer last year. We’d been together for 16 years, since I was 21 and he was 23. I had given birth to our only child three weeks before his diagnosis. My son was just shy of 10 months old when his dad died, and he’s now turned two.I loved my late partner deeply and had planned to stay with him for ever. We were embarking on an 18-year project together, raising our son. Now I think, how can I ever be happy again? Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Is sisterhood the secret to a long life? The Sardinian village that could hold key to women’s longevity

primary_source.headline: Is sisterhood the secret to a long life? The Sardinian village that could hold key to women’s longevity
primary_source.content: Meet some of the elderly residents of Bolotana, in line to be the world’s sixth ‘blue zone’ for its high number of female centenariansWhen Giovanna Marras opens the door to her home in Bolotana, a mountain village in central Sardinia, her eyes are bright with curiosity as she sizes up her visitors. Her sister, Mariangela, peeks out too, soon ushering her guests inside and handing out dishes of ice-cream. The sisters are full of life, talking animatedly. Giovanna is 101 and Mariangela is 99.Sitting in their living room, Giovanna swiftly recaps her life story: she excelled at school before moving to Cagliari, the capital of the Italian island, at 18 to train as a seamstress. The sisters went on to run a successful tailoring business in Bolotana before travelling the world after retirement. Neither married. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Braam! How the music in The Traitors plays with your emotions

primary_source.headline: Braam! How the music in The Traitors plays with your emotions
primary_source.content: Watch: How does music on The Traitors manipulate your emotions? But the shadowiest of the show's shadowy secrets is its music. Have you ever noticed how the soundtrack manipulates your perception? A sinister orchestral flourish hints at a double cross. A cheeky chord injects humour into a kitchen conflab. As ever, though, you shouldn't trust what happens in the castle. The music can provide emphasis or act as misdirection, all at the producers' behest. Duplicity was baked into the music from the beginning. "I remember the BBC was quite reluctant to even think about a show with murder as a main feature, so I knew I didn't want the music to go really dark," says Sam Watts, who composed the opening theme and much of the incidental score (but is not responsible for the show's haunting cover versions of well-known pop songs... more on those later).

stories.primary_headline: Top Turkish pop group go from reality TV to Wembley in one turbulent year

primary_source.headline: Top Turkish pop group go from reality TV to Wembley in one turbulent year
primary_source.content: manifest performed their first UK concert at Wembley Arena The six band members are clutching union jack umbrellas as they pose for press photographs and mingle with British pop acts, including K-pop-trained boyband dearALICE. Netflix cameras are filming the evening for a six-part documentary. The group are in London hoping to build on their success in Turkey and reach an international audience. Their ambitions come after a turbulent year at home, during which the band were prosecuted for public indecency over their outfits and dance moves during a concert in Istanbul. A few weeks after their appearance on the boat, I meet the group again at Wembley Arena, where they are preparing for their first UK concert the following night. As the staging - complete with giant LED screens and the group's logo - is set up around them, the six members rehearse synchronised choreography alongside their back-up dancers.
